chunks: From him, from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man whom we invited to the totality of what we are upon from the totality of Islam, and he affirmed it, then he drank wine, committed fornication, and consumed usury, while nothing of the halal and the haram had been explained to him—should the hadd be carried out upon him if he was ignorant of it? He said: So he said, “No, unless there is established against him clear proof that he had already acknowledged their prohibition.”

key_terms.الرِّبَا: usury, unlawful gain through interest-based increase
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, the religion into which the man was invited and which he accepted in general
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine or intoxicant whose consumption is prohibited
key_terms.بَيِّنَةٌ: clear proof or legally probative evidence

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd punishment applied to someone who committed a forbidden act without knowing it was haram?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a legal hadd punishment is not established against a person who committed prohibited acts while ignorant of their prohibition, unless proof exists that he had already acknowledged that those acts were forbidden. It emphasizes the juridical relevance of knowledge and prior recognition of tahrim before enforcement of the hadd.
